title: Pay, time and money in the police and sheriff complaint files
question: Do the civilian complaint files hold allegations about overtime, timecards, pay, outside work, City time or property, or theft by officers, and how were they resolved?
finding: None of 7,350 police allegations (2,837 cases) or 357 Sheriff's Office allegations (90 cases) concerns overtime, timecards, pay or outside work. The nearest, 26 allegations of absence from post, inattention, alcohol on duty or misuse of City equipment, had none sustained of 11 decided on the merits. Of 13 police complaints saying an officer took money or property or sought a bribe, none was sustained (8 had a merits finding; at the 6.0% case baseline, none sustained has a 61% chance); 4 went to the Police Department's Internal Affairs Division.
how: One row per allegation (latest snapshot). Every narrative and allegation summary searched for overtime, timecard, time sheet, payroll, secondary or outside employment, 10B, sick leave, City time. Groups are fixed allegation wordings. The officer-took group was chosen by reading every narrative mentioning theft, stealing, money, cash, bribes or personal use. A merits finding is sustained, unfounded, proper conduct, insufficient evidence or exonerated.
limits: These are complaints, mostly from the public, about conduct on the street or in the jails. Pay, overtime and outside work are handled inside each department and by the Controller, so their absence here does not show such problems are absent. A complaint about money taken during an arrest is often disputed and hard to prove either way; referrals to Internal Affairs have their outcome recorded elsewhere. The files carry no discipline column.

rows.group: Time and City resources (absent from post, inattentive, alcohol on duty, misuse of City equipment)
Money and property handling (seized money or property, booking property, found property for personal use)
Truthfulness (misrepresented the truth, false statement or charges, undisclosed facts, compromised investigation)
Misuse of authority or records (misused authority, database access, unauthorized disclosure)
Narrative says an officer took money or property, sought a bribe or used City property for personal use (hand-read)
All Sheriff's Office allegations (Inspector General file)
